newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares down, brokers say trend to stay.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares down, brokers say trend to stay.

text.p: Shares and turnover slid on Friday and brokers said they expected little change next week for the struggling market.
"It's not quite stable," said Robertas Berzinskas, a broker with Vilniaus Bank.
"The market has been going down since the beginning of this week, especially the A list. I think the situation will be the same next week," he said.
Brokers said this week was one they would sooner forget, with suspensions of some of the most popular shares on the bourse hampering activity.
The official index fell 12.45 points to 909.56 points, while group A shares slipped 5.66 points to 1936.63 points.
Central market turnover was a dull 493,000 litas, down from 634,000 litas yesterday. Block trading volume was also down, at about one million litas from 13.6 million litas.
"The market's going nowhere," said Kestutis Kupshys, a broker with Mendes Prior Europe.
Hermis Bank was the most active on the central market, turning over 217,000 litas at 180.00 litas. Its price was unchanged.
Brokers have high hopes for Hermis Bank due to positive results for the first four months of the year. They say its shares are cheap compared to the more expensive Vilniaus Bank.
Vilniaus Bank dropped to 230.00 litas from 240.00 litas on the central market amid low turnover of 10,810 litas.
Vilniaus Bank was more active in block trades, turning over 920,000 litas at 230.00 litas.
